correctness.rationale: The quadratic energy identity isolates every edge coefficient on simple graphs. Every neighbor pair on a 2-vertex-connected graph closes to a cycle, so cycle circulations force equality along even walks; connected graph parity then gives exactly 2 invariant dimensions if bipartite and 1 otherwise. The checkerboard is annihilated by each face's central average, and weighted skew-adjointness gives conservation of its component during every Crank–Nicolson step. Cauchy–Schwarz in inverse-Laplacian metric yields the floor; an even-periodic Cartesian checkerboard saturates it. Nine exact-rational graph fixtures and a 4-by-6 Laplacian identity were replayed, while universal statements rest on the analytic argument.

value.rationale: A complete graph-topology criterion determines precisely when all centered divergence-free face controls share an inaccessible nonconstant tracer mode, with an exact tight inverse-Laplacian lower bound on any optimal mixing objective. It reveals a structural unmixability mechanism even under exact mass and L2 conservation, extending beyond ordinary grid-oscillation warnings. The target invariant and bound are natural to the motivating numerical scheme, not arbitrarily chosen finite data.
